runner: khg_contracts.store.conformance.run(factory, *, only=None, capabilities=None) -> EARL-shaped report (passed, failed, inapplicable, cantTell per scenario)
factory: factory(schema: Schema, clock: Clock) -> a fresh, empty Store

clock.rule: one tick per write call; a step's 'at' sets the clock; later ticks continue from it

requires: the capabilities a scenario needs: those of the operations and assertions under test (valid_time for as_of, valid_mode or end_validity; transaction_time for as_at or get(version); history_export for content history; atomic_writes for a multi-record write), plus the data flags of the records it writes or loads (literal_values, special_values, goals, nesting, ordered_roles). A scenario that loads @fixture needs all five data flags; its core variant (id suffix c) loads @fixture[core] and needs only literal_values and nesting. A store lacking a flag gets 'inapplicable', never 'failed'.
given: put steps run one call each (one record per call, in the listed order, for a store without atomic_writes); apply steps run one event; load loads a container into the empty store

references.@<id>: the fixture record with that id
references.@entities: every entity record of the fixture
references.@fixture[core]: the fixture without the records that need ordered_roles, special_values or goals (f:route-1, f:born-scribe, f:cat-7, g:who-1774)
references.@<id>.<field>: that field of the fixture record

patch_keys.set_binding: replace the value of the binding with that bid
patch_keys.drop_bindings: remove bindings by bid, and those bids from every evidence supports list
patch_keys.set_evidence: change fields of the evidence record with that id

pattern: find patterns are [{role, value, position?}] where value is a C1 value, {"any": true} or {"any_unbound": true}; a missing position matches any position; [] matches every fact of the relation

then.select + equals: a projection of the result equals the value (ids, value, version, versions, status, status_ref, goal, record, canonical, receipt.records, receipt.warnings, evidence.ids, evidence.<id>.<field>, binding.<bid>.<field>, derived.<field>, terminal, terminal.ids, steps.count, record.<id>.<field>, versions.<id>, header.<field>, metadata.<field>, node.<id>.<path>); '{store_id}' in an expected string is the store's id
then.error + info: the call raises; the code is among the error's codes; info matches as a subset (objects: listed keys; lists: same length, element-wise)
then.container_equals: the export equals that container (header without created_at and generator; records in canonical form), ignoring the listed store-assigned fields
then.hif_valid: the export passes the vendored HIF schema and the khg-hif profile
then.equals_file: the export equals that file, ignoring the listed attrs keys
then.reload_equal: loading the export into a fresh store and exporting again gives the same bytes
then.deterministic: two fresh runs give byte-identical output

projections.canonical: the record in canonical form without version, recorded_at, recorded_by
projections.derived.<field>: computed by the runner from the returned record (derived is an optional cache)
projections.receipt.records: [id, version, outcome] per written record, sorted by id; outcome created, versioned or noop
projections.receipt.warnings: [{code, ids}] lint findings of the write (KHG-L008 possible overlaps)

scenarios.title: put then get returns the record
an identical put is a no-op
one invalid record in a batch writes nothing
a candidate never enters a store
put reports the validator's code
optimistic concurrency: a stale expect is refused
unbound is accepted in a goal and refused elsewhere
put cannot change the status of an existing id
a reference to an entity the store does not hold is refused
a value naming a redirected entity is refused (redirects are rewritten in 1.2)
each write makes a version; get(as_at) returns the older one
add_evidence makes a new version with the same content
adding an end date is a refinement; changing a core binding is refused
precedent: judge probe: C accepted Bob for Alice as version 2

scenarios.title: a new version that rewrites earlier evidence is refused
a transition outside the table (retracted to disputed) is refused
superseded content is frozen
a somevalue binding refined to a value keeps its bid
entity versions: labels may change, types only grow, redirect_to is set once
end_validity may replace a novalue end (a world change): the status stays asserted
incident is complete and in id order; goals are not asserted
a node in two roles returns the fact once; the role filter
default reads hide superseded, quoted, deprecated, goal and lifecycle records
the status filter can include superseded facts
incident on a fact id finds nesting and lifecycle records
keyset pagination is stable
degree equals the length of incident
find at_least matches a multiset; a repeated role needs distinct bindings
find exact needs the whole binding multiset
find by a time literal: precision takes part in equality; the calendar does not
quantities match with unit and bounds
ordered roles match by position; a pattern without a position matches any position
an any_unbound pattern finds goals, which appear only when asked for
find matches novalue
get ignores the Where filters
get_many returns every requested record in one call
timeless relations pass every as_of filter, in both modes
an empty pattern lists the relation's facts, paginated
vocabulary ids (units, globes, rank reasons) are not nodes: incident finds nothing
as_of filters by valid time; an ended fact stays asserted
as_at before a supersession sees the older belief; so does the walk
definite and possible readings at year precision
as_of and as_at compose
an undated fact: definite reads skip it, possible reads and reads without as_of keep it
end_validity keeps the status and adds the end binding
a Julian date is compared on the proleptic Gregorian line
an end-only (until) fact has no definite validity: the start is unknown
a somevalue end (ended, date unknown) has no definite validity after the start window
precision 7 is an ordinal century: +1900/7 is 1801-1900
precision 6 is an ordinal millennium; precision 8 is a decade
a BCE Julian date: historical year -44 is astronomical -43, and Julian 15 March is Gregorian 13 March
precedent: critique CONS-01 (Wikibase: BCE years use historical numbering)

scenarios.title: a put that breaks the key invariant raises KeyCollision and writes nothing
find_by_key without as_of returns the key's timeline in id order
find_by_key with as_of returns the holder at that time
one preferred fact may stand beside normal ones on a key
a deprecated fact never collides and is hidden by default
a non-temporal key collides whatever the dates
close_older on a succession: the caller ends the older fact at the newer start, then puts
dispute: one transition writes the new fact, both statuses and the khg:disputes record
a year-precision handover is a succession, not a collision; the possible overlap is a warning
a transition back to asserted drops status_ref and re-checks the key
a special value in a key role gives no key digest and never collides
precedent: judge re-run: C's digest made two somevalue keys collide

scenarios.title: an undated fact beside a dated one on a temporal key: no collision, a possible-overlap warning
precedent: critique SEM-08, CONS-11 (open question X3, ruled)

scenarios.title: two undated facts on one temporal key: no collision, a possible-overlap warning
same start (R01 case 3b): close_older does not apply, the action is dispute
backfill (X4): the incoming fact is the older one, so it is the one closed
a refining claim on the same key is a merge: it becomes a new version of the stored fact
a new claim on a disputed key joins the dispute
one put spanning two relations reports every collision with its own policy
key literals compare exactly: 2019 at year precision and 30 June 2019 are different keys
supersede is one event; the walk forward ends at the current belief
the walk runs backward
the walk branches on conflation
a superseding fact must be asserted when the event runs, so events cannot form a cycle
precedent: B S053 (cycle, KHG-D012 stays a container check)

scenarios.title: put cannot create a record in status superseded
retraction writes khg:retracts; a retracted fact does not come back
retracting a supersession record restores the superseded fact (undo) and drops its status_ref
binding a goal slot is a new version with the same bid
a fully bound goal becomes asserted by a transition that drops the goal block
a goal with an unbound slot cannot become asserted
an asserted fact cannot become a goal
a supersession chain A -> B -> C: the walk's terminal is C, whose predecessors stay superseded
undoing a keyed correction must resolve the superseding fact, here by a dispute
a new version of a superseding fact must keep the correction's key digest
precedent: critique SEM-11 (put runs D011 on new versions of superseding facts)
